title: Use relative dates with multiple time zones upon date difference
line: Other time zones in the clock's popup and tooltip now say "tomorrow" or "yesterday" when their day differs from yours.
explanation: The reporter's 6.6 build appended the full date to times in other time zones whose day differed from the local one; current master appends the weekday name instead ("4:32 AM Sunday"), which still makes you work out whether that is tomorrow or yesterday. formatTime() in main.qml, used by both the popup's Time Zones list and the tooltip, now computes the calendar-day difference from the local date and shows "%1 tomorrow" or "%1 yesterday" (translatable, with context), keeping the weekday only for the rare two-day gap (e.g. UTC+14 vs UTC-12).

commits.message:
applets/digital-clock: say tomorrow or yesterday for other time zones

Times in other time zones that fall on a different day were followed by
the weekday name, which makes you work out how it relates to today. Show
"tomorrow" or "yesterday" instead, keeping the weekday for larger gaps.

BUG: 518383

media.caption: Popup on master, local time Saturday evening in Rome: Tokyo and Kiritimati show "Sunday"
Same popup with the fix: they show "tomorrow"
Session running in UTC+14 (Sunday morning): Los Angeles shows "Saturday"
Same with the fix: Los Angeles shows "yesterday"; Tokyo, on the same day, shows no label

review.text: Clean, minimal QML change in applets/digital-clock/main.qml that computes the exact calendar-day difference via Date.UTC() (handling month/year boundaries and DST properly) and shows translatable "%1 tomorrow" / "%1 yesterday" strings with clear i18nc context while preserving the weekday fallback for rare two-day gaps. Because both the popup's Time Zones list and the tooltip use formatTime(), both places are covered consistently, and the before/after screenshots verify tomorrow, yesterday, and same-day cases.
